prompt:
A particle moves along the $x$-axis so that its position at time $t\ge0$ is $s(t)=t^3-6t^2+9t+2$.

**(a)** Find $v(t)$ and $a(t)$. At what times is the particle at rest, and at which of those times does it change direction? Justify your answer.

**(b)** For $0\le t\le5$, find all intervals on which the particle is speeding up. Justify your answer.

**(c)** Find the total distance traveled by the particle from $t=0$ to $t=5$.

**(d)** Find the greatest speed of the particle on $0\le t\le5$, and the time at which it occurs.

rubric.description: (a) Shows $v$ changes sign at both times (positive, negative, positive), so the particle changes direction at both
(b) Finds the sign of $a(t)$: negative for $t<2$, positive for $t>2$
(b) Concludes the particle speeds up on $(1,2)$ and $(3,5)$, because $v$ and $a$ have the same sign there
(d) Compares $|v|$ at the endpoints and at $t=2$ (where $a=0$): $9,3,24$
(d) Concludes the greatest speed is 24 at $t=5$

sampleResponse:
(a) $v(t)=3t^2-12t+9=3(t-1)(t-3)$ and $a(t)=6t-12$. The particle is at rest at $t=1$ and $t=3$. $v>0$ on $[0,1)$, $v<0$ on $(1,3)$ and $v>0$ on $(3,\infty)$, so $v$ changes sign at both times and the particle changes direction at both.
(b) The particle speeds up when $v$ and $a$ have the same sign. $a<0$ for $t<2$ and $a>0$ for $t>2$. On $(0,1)$: $v>0$, $a<0$ (slowing). On $(1,2)$: $v<0$, $a<0$ (speeding up). On $(2,3)$: $v<0$, $a>0$ (slowing). On $(3,5)$: $v>0$, $a>0$ (speeding up). The particle speeds up on $(1,2)$ and $(3,5)$.
(c) $s(0)=2$, $s(1)=6$, $s(3)=2$, $s(5)=22$. Distance $=4+4+20=28$.
(d) $v'(t)=a(t)=0$ at $t=2$, where $v(2)=-3$. Compare $|v(0)|=9$, $|v(2)|=3$, $|v(5)|=24$. The greatest speed is 24 at $t=5$.

prompt:
A 25-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall. The bottom of the ladder slides away from the wall at a constant rate of 2 feet per second. Let $x$ be the distance from the bottom of the ladder to the wall and $y$ the height of the top of the ladder, both in feet.

**(a)** Write an equation relating $x$ and $y$. At the instant $x=7$, how fast is the top of the ladder sliding down the wall?

**(b)** At the instant $x=7$, is the area of the triangle formed by the ladder, the wall and the ground increasing or decreasing? Find the rate of change of the area at that instant.

**(c)** Let $\theta$ be the angle between the ladder and the ground. Find $\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}$ at the instant $x=7$.

**(d)** The tangent line to $y=\sqrt{625-x^2}$ at $x=7$ is used to approximate the height when $x=7.5$. Find this approximation, and say whether it is an overestimate or an underestimate. Justify your answer.

rubric.description: (a) Differentiates to get $\frac{dy}{dt}=-\frac{7}{12}$ ft/s (sliding down at $\frac7{12}$ ft/s)
(b) Evaluates $\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac{527}{24}>0$, so the area is increasing
(c) Uses $\cos\theta=\frac{x}{25}$ and differentiates, finding $\sin\theta=\frac{24}{25}$ at that instant
(d) Says overestimate because $y$ is concave down ($y''<0$)

sampleResponse:
(a) $x^2+y^2=625$. At $x=7$, $y=24$. Differentiating, $2x\frac{dx}{dt}+2y\frac{dy}{dt}=0$, so $\frac{dy}{dt}=-\frac{x}{y}\frac{dx}{dt}=-\frac{7}{24}(2)=-\frac7{12}$ ft/s. The top slides down at $\frac7{12}$ ft/s.
(b) $A=\frac12xy$, so $\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac12\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\,y+x\frac{dy}{dt}\right)=\frac12\left(2\cdot24+7\cdot\left(-\frac7{12}\right)\right)=\frac12\left(48-\frac{49}{12}\right)=\frac{527}{24}$ square feet per second. This is positive, so the area is increasing.
(c) $\cos\theta=\frac x{25}$, so $-\sin\theta\frac{d\theta}{dt}=\frac1{25}\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac2{25}$. At $x=7$, $\sin\theta=\frac{24}{25}$, so $\frac{d\theta}{dt}=-\frac{2/25}{24/25}=-\frac1{12}$ rad/s.
(d) The tangent line at $x=7$ is $L(x)=24-\frac7{24}(x-7)$, so $L(7.5)=24-\frac{7}{48}=\frac{1145}{48}\approx23.85$. The function $y=\sqrt{625-x^2}$ is concave down ($y''=-\frac{625}{(625-x^2)^{3/2}}<0$), so its graph lies below its tangent lines and the approximation is an overestimate.
